knowledge_gaps: Frequency matching is inconsistent: substitutes matched to recent items are reused for random positions whose original items may have different frequencies. This confounds position with corruption severity. Specify matching for both conditions, substitute assignment, duplicate handling, and sparse-bin fallback.

Replacement preserves occupied positions and input masks, but changes content-dependent attention and gates. It cannot isolate attention geometry or establish that stronger recency weighting would improve recommendations.

Reproduction requires fixed corruption counts, k-selection rules, minimum history length, frequency bins, user selection, tie handling, nonfinite-score handling, bootstrap settings, and a diagnostic runtime cap. Define category-level aggregation and the equally weighted four-category macro estimate.

The diagnostic measures sensitivity rather than the reported compatibility or purchase-purpose failures. Originality 6 and potential 8 lack supporting comparisons; difficulty 3 overlooks matched corruption and uncertainty estimation. In-sample targets and repeated diagnostic-guided selection also require prospective validation.
